human_summary: Final auto-trader transaction-envelope guard over host-projected booleans for request presence, paired arguments, bounds validation, and allowed stream scope.
assumptions: The host computes the boolean projection for sequence, expiration, fee, and stream-scope checks before Tau evaluation.
The explicit assurance domain exhaustively enumerates the full boolean input product over i1..i9.
The live submit lane treats o4 as the authoritative admissibility bit for the final Tau transaction envelope.

intended_preconditions: Idle traces with tx_requested = 0 are admissible and intentionally keep all outputs high.
Requested transactions may only pass when argument pairing, bounds checks, and stream-scope checks all succeed.

analysis_partitions.intent: The idle lane is always admissible.
Requested transactions without both paired arguments must reject.
Requested transactions with invalid sequence, expiration, or fee bounds must reject.
Requested transactions with wrong stream scope must reject.

outputs.name: o2
outputs.contract_expr: 1 if (i1 == 0 or (i4 == 1 and i5 == 1 and i6 == 1)) else 0

outputs.name: o3
outputs.contract_expr: 1 if (i1 == 0 or (i7 == 1 and i8 == 1 and i9 == 1)) else 0

outputs.name: o4
outputs.contract_expr: 1 if (i1 == 0 or (i2 == 1 and i3 == 1 and i4 == 1 and i5 == 1 and i6 == 1 and i7 == 1 and i8 == 1 and i9 == 1)) else 0

theorems.statement: For all inputs in the explicit boolean domain, o4 = 1 implies either an idle trace or a requested transaction with paired args, validated bounds, and allowed stream scope.
For all inputs in the explicit boolean domain, idle traces and fully valid requested transactions force o4 = 1.
Distinct autotrader_tx_envelope_guard_v1 output-vector regions are pairwise disjoint over the explicit boolean domain.
The autotrader_tx_envelope_guard_v1 behavior atlas covers the full explicit boolean domain.
The contract semantics and the Tau binary agree on the explicit autotrader_tx_envelope_guard_v1 boolean domain.

evidence_links.note: Explicit boolean-domain parity cases for the transaction-envelope guard.
Independent shadow semantics for the requested-envelope policy.
